name: http
doc:
An HTTP request, and the one thing you do with it.

Every platform has this and every platform calls it something else. The point of writing it down here is that the name is the only part that differs: `curl`, `fetch`, `requests.request` and `reqwest` all take a method, a URL, some headers and a body, and all give back a status, some headers and a body. Once that is said once, it has an address, and the address is the same everywhere.

types.name: Method
types.doc: The verbs, as the ones that exist rather than as free text.

types.name: Request
types.doc: What every one of these platforms takes, under whatever name it uses.

fields.name: headers
fields.doc: Names are matched case-insensitively by the protocol; they are carried here as written.

fields.name: body
fields.doc: Bytes rather than text: a body is not always text, and deciding that it is loses files.

types.name: Response
types.doc: What every one of them gives back.

functions.name: request
functions.doc:
Send one request, get one response.

This is the proposition. `curl`, `fetch`, `requests.request` and `reqwest` are proofs of it — the same claim, proved four times in four places. A future, because none of them answer immediately and pretending otherwise is how the asynchrony leaks back out later.
